controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Colour from Gaia's spectrum of the star; darkening toward the edge fitted here to TESS transits of HD 189733b. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The colour of Gaia DR3's measured spectrum. The edge darkening is fitted to 30 TESS transits (600–1000 nm): the edge is about a third as bright as the centre. The axis is tilted about 14° from the planet's orbit, as measured. Two separate spot interpretations are available: one published hypothetical activity pattern and one dated transit-chord candidate. No measured global map exists.

controls.label: Spot model
controls.qualification: A published hypothetical dense-spot-band layout from Narrett, Rackham & de Wit (2024), Figure 7 left. Their HST spectral model gives 42% mean spot coverage, and their TESS-band spot/photosphere intensity ratio is 0.099. This is an illustrative arrangement, not an observed surface map; the pattern is stationary.
controls.notes: Narrett, Rackham & de Wit (2024), Figure 7 left, illustrates one possible dense latitudinal spot distribution for HD 189733 A. The paper estimates 42 ± 4% mean spot coverage from HST spectra and a 0.099 TESS-band spot/photosphere intensity ratio. Its figure is a hypothetical model, not a resolved stellar image. The white transit-guide lines are omitted. Spot contrast is applied achromatically to Gaia's measured colour, and the limb plate does not rotate.

controls.label: 2021 spot
controls.qualification: Static reconstruction of one TESS spot-crossing candidate in HD 189733b transit 2165. The paper gives a minimum 5° angular radius and 7.6% TESS-band contrast; position along the transit chord comes from its timing and the hosted orbit. Shape, sky orientation and Gaia-colour application are display assumptions.
controls.notes: Haris et al. (2025), Table 3, transit 2165 at BJD-2450000 9435.46: event midpoint +1890 s, minimum angular radius 5.0°, contrast 0.076. This is a single candidate dark region along the planet’s path, shown on a fixed camera-facing limb plate. It is not a resolved surface image, global map or time-varying rotation. TESS-band darkness is displayed achromatically over the Gaia-colour photosphere.
